study.question: Observation: the task/item incumbent has click AUC 0.6558817596 versus DIN 0.6555440824. Adding feedback to its selector reduces click AUC to 0.6554607825 (-0.0004209770), while increasing cart/fav/buy AUC by 0.0030511571/0.0075038493/0.0034418316. With shared routing, feedback instead improves click by 0.0002638150. Task routing gains 0.0006321967 in the item-only branch but -0.0000525953 in the feedback branch. Thus prior task routing has a mixed, single-seed result rather than repeated mechanism support. No failed execution is listed; the full feedback candidate nevertheless failed to beat the click incumbent. Code inspection shows all four objectives update the same score trunk and embeddings. Does restricting direct selector-trunk updates to click preserve feedback utility without the observed click tradeoff?
study.hypothesis: The shared history selector may face incompatible task demands when feedback enters its score features. Keep shared embeddings, four trainable task score rows and all forward information, but make the selector hidden representation primary-anchored by stopping auxiliary gradients immediately before their readout. Auxiliary tasks still train their readout rows/towers and shared embeddings through pooled values, context and target. The proposed cause is a hypothesis: no local gradient-angle or task-dominance measurement is available. This specifically tests direct selector backward flow; it neither isolates every embedding update nor changes the scalar objective.

nearest_work.difference: STEM primary Method, All Forward Task-specific Backward, Eq. (4), explicitly stops gradients from other-task expert outputs while sharing them forward. We inherit the general separation of forward and backward sharing, but use a single embedding collection and single history score trunk with primary-only trunk gradients, not STEM task-specific embedding/expert groups or all-expert gating. This is a local adaptation; originality is unverified. Publisher PDF access was denied; the arXiv v2 full method text was available and inspected.

The PCGrad primary abstract describes projection of conflicting task gradients. This candidate performs fixed asymmetric stop-gradient at one representation boundary, with no gradient comparisons/projection, optimizer override, or multiple backward passes. Abstract inspection is not full algorithm or implementation verification; no PCGrad reproduction is claimed.

Original v1 primary text at https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11565v1, sections 3.1-3.2, describes task/sequence/categorical tokens and proxy information exchange. Our inherited task-indexed history compression is far simpler; this proposal tests backward routing, without adding task tokens, hub broadcasts or stacked interaction. Primary-paper transfer to the local benchmark remains unproven.

Pinned commit 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d, lines 123-158, initializes task sequence hubs using multi_masks and stacks interactions. We retain the local retrieval ancestor and do not import the task-mask pooling or benchmark hub implementation.

Archived primary text describes target-conditioned local activation and weighted pooling. Field embeddings, target/history interactions, unnormalized pooling and Dice come from the existing four-task adaptation. We do not assert an exact original DIN reproduction.

inherited_components: FeatureEmbeddingDict, target-item interaction features, masked history keys/action values, shared 64/32 Dice score trunk, four score rows initially identical and four 128/64 Dice towers.

Original frozen data identity 9f110bfc2f037f36e2f48787b812df640fe5df2de1cda8db7ac04590c1c9be44 and protocol are host-owned; prior successful receipts are reused as starting evidence, not independently reverified parquet inputs in this coding environment.
Known stop-gradient separation of forward sharing and backward ownership (STEM); fixed localized primary anchoring is an adaptation, not a verified new principle.
study.proposed_difference: Add selector_gradient in {joint,primary}. For H=score_trunk(interactions), primary mode computes the click row from W*H+b and auxiliary rows from W*stop_gradient(H)+b using the same four-row readout. A boolean label-derived buffer selects the click row; it has no trainable parameters. The ordinary four-task forward values and loss remain unchanged at fixed weights; only direct auxiliary gradients through the selector are removed. Feedback-in-score is crossed with this choice. Four standalone files include their literal CONFIG and constructor defaults. joint controls match historical arms functionally; rerunning them checks implementation comparability and is charged, not independent evidence. In no-grad inference every arm uses the original single readout. No filesystem/network operations or new inputs are added.
predictions: At fixed weights, each joint/primary pair has equal parameter count and forward predictions within BF16 tolerance; only the intended backward paths differ. All four should have the inherited 32,060,552 parameters if the same feature map is used. Host must measure rather than trust this expectation.

D_feedback is positive and at least 0.0002 in click AUC if this intervention yields a practically useful first-seed rescue. Auxiliary mean AUC should decrease by no more than 0.001 relative to joint_feedback; report every individual task regardless. These are predeclared triage thresholds, not significance tests.
I=D_feedback-D_item should be positive for a feedback-specific effect; similar gains in both branches instead suggest a broader selector optimization effect.

Predeclared descriptive history bins are empty, 1-16, 17-64 and >64, matching historical receipts. Report samples/positives/negatives and AUC/Logloss; empty history has only 6,444 samples and 427 positives, so it is low precision. Do not demand zero empty-history effect, because shared embeddings can change. Any additional unavailable slice/cluster interval is recorded unavailable rather than fabricated.

All four arms use identical data passes; parameter count and no-grad inference structure match. Training runtime/peak memory may differ because the backward graph changes; measured quality-cost tradeoffs must accompany equal-recipe comparisons.
falsifiers: No click gain or a reversal in primary_feedback relative to its joint control fails to support this implementation of selector-gradient isolation as a remedy; one null run does not refute all gradient interference.
A nonpositive I fails to support a specifically feedback-related interaction even if primary anchoring has a main effect.
Click gains accompanied by auxiliary mean degradation beyond the predeclared tolerance fail the joint rescue prediction and must be reported as a task tradeoff.

Gradient-path, masking or parameter-equality failures invalidate attribution. Equal gains from item-only isolation weaken a feedback-specific explanation. Lack of repeated paired-seed support leaves every effectiveness claim preliminary.
alternative_explanations: Prior differences may be random single-seed/order/initialization variation; all historical trajectories were successful executions and none is a repeated result.
Feedback may encode an inappropriate similarity signal for click, regardless of gradient conflict. Primary gradients cannot necessarily repair an unsuitable forward representation.

Auxiliary labels are user/category/brand matches within 24 hours, not ad-specific conversions. Their different semantics can explain competing representation demands without establishing a universal mechanism.

Primary anchoring changes gradient magnitude and dense clipping as well as task direction; reduced regularization/noise or loss balance at this module can explain a gain. Direct angle/norm diagnostics and a subsequent scale control would be needed for a conflict claim.
Shared embedding paths, Dice running statistics and score-row adaptation still transmit auxiliary effects indirectly. No claim of complete task independence is justified.

Official offline history may contain delayed feedback that would be unavailable online; released whole-window vocabularies/static snapshots remain benchmark limitations, and any result is limited to this frozen offline setting.

Four arms predict roughly 1,400s observed-recipe wall; conservatively reserve 4*481.348=1,925.391s, capped by host at 4*1203.369=4,813.476s plus all preparation/diagnostics/failed costs. Local checking initially failed on a literal list-versus-tuple default comparison; normalizing sequence types corrected the checker and all source/config/schema checks then passed. No model execution occurred. Its preparation time remains charged.
cost_plan.attribution_reserve: All four submitted arms count, including the two historical-control reruns. Reserve at least 4,000 additional wall seconds for numerical graph/masking diagnostics and a consequential scale or representation-sharing control if authorized. Reserve another 6*481.348=2,888.088s for two extra paired seeds of candidate plus two closest controls if the direction survives (host scheduling only); repeats use identical seeds across compared arms. If a claim needs a further control, allocate it before asserting the mechanism.
cost_plan.assessment_reserve: Keep at least 10,000 wall seconds for final frozen comparison suite, repetitions/assessment overhead and failure handling. No held-out request in this phase. Before later withheld scoring freeze source/config/checkpoint hashes, selected candidates, closest reference/ablations, seeds and commands. Closed assessment results must never enter open selection or a reused-holdout memory.
cost_plan.stop_rule: Host owns all training/scoring, ledger and hard caps. Do not alter the recipe, split, labels, scorer or limits. Count all preparation, local checks, diagnostics, controls, failures and retries. Stop for budget/user/integrity limits or if no discriminating admissible experiment fits while preserving reserves. If a trial execution state is unknown, inspect its authorized receipt rather than automatically duplicating it; no failure is present at entry.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Prior declared use produced executed task-score retrieval arms, but feedback-aware task routing did not improve click. This is mixed local evidence, not a confirmation of INFNet or a causal estimate of external knowledge value. Full token/hub replacement would confound the immediate selector backward-flow question.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: No new hub or token component adopted; prior task-score rows are retained while a separate gradient-routing adaptation is tested.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Single local-activation pooling stage with selectively blocked backward paths versus stacked task/proxy token interactions and gated broadcasts. Original v1 text and pinned benchmark forward code checked separately.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If the controlled backward intervention fails, do not credit INFNet-inspired task scoring for a nonexistent rescue; consider a separately controlled token/hub architecture only if new evidence justifies it.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Activation sparsity after pooling is an alternative explanation/remedy for interference, but no local activation-interference evidence exists. The previous round deferred this intervention and the new AUC tradeoff still does not isolate it.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None adopted; no competitive sparse filter or multi-view fusion added.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Candidate changes direct auxiliary gradient access to the selector rather than sparsifying forward activations after pooling. Original SSR paper is unaudited; card provenance does not establish local utility.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: If selector anchoring fails and downstream redundant/interfering activations are measured, reconsider SSR with matched dense replacement controls; no such effectiveness claim is made now.
